title: Flow definition
description: A declarative flow, as the official definitions repository publishes it (03-arquitectura.md, section 9). The generic engine executes it, so a new flow is new data rather than new code — which is what makes the flows of later phases a distribution problem instead of a release. The initialization flow of M1 is the first one distributed. This document declares what a flow is; flow-progress.schema.json records what happened when one ran, and the two meet at the stage identifier.

name.description: How the catalog names this flow. Not translated: the marketplace card shows it before anybody installs it.

description.description: What this flow is for, in the languages the marketplace shows.

requiredCapabilities.description: What a provider must offer for this flow to run. Declared here and indexed by the manifest, which T-060 generates from the definitions.

stages.description: The stages, in the order they are meant to run. Uniqueness of the identifiers among them is checked by the core: it is a rule between siblings of one document, and uniqueItems does not catch it — two stages with the same id and different content would pass.

blockingData.description: The checklist this flow exists to fill. Stages resolve what they can; at closure the engine computes what is still missing and asks directly for the gaps only (T-072), and a complete checklist is what enables the deterministic scaffold.

stage.description: One stage of the flow, declaring the six things a stage declares (03-arquitectura.md, section 9): its purpose, who takes part, what it reads, what it produces, whether it can be skipped, and which blocking data it resolves. The state machine a stage moves through belongs to the progress artifact, not here.

purpose.description: What this stage is for, shown to whoever is running the flow.

participants.description: The roles that take part, never the agents: a project binds each role to the agent it declared for it, so a flow keeps working when a team swaps one architect definition for another. An empty list is a statement rather than an omission — the stage is deterministic and the platform itself executes it, which is what the scaffold stage is. In M1 the same machinery runs with a single participant; the turn protocol and its agenda arrive in M2 without changing this contract.

inputs.description: What this stage reads. The engine resolves it through the documentary index rather than walking the filesystem, which is what makes a stage able to read what earlier ones wrote without knowing where it landed.

stages.description: Earlier stages of this same flow, whose outputs feed this one. That they name stages that exist is checked by the core.

tags.description: Anything in the index carrying these tags — among them a document the user brought to the flow rather than one a stage produced.

outputs.description: The artifacts closing this stage produces. The agent's structured output is validated against the schema of the artifact type named here, and a failure that survives the bounded retries leaves the stage pending_closure (T-071).

skippable.description: Whether the user may skip this stage. Skipping is not free: the blocking data the stage would have resolved is asked for directly at closure.

resolves.description: The blocking-data keys this stage is expected to fill. That they name entries this flow declares is checked by the core.

output.description: One artifact a stage produces. The type is the schema: naming task here means the extraction is validated against task.schema.json, so a separate schema field would only be a second name for the same thing, free to disagree with the first.

tags.description: Tags stamped on what this stage produces, so a later stage can ask the index for it.

blockingDatum.description: One entry of the checklist. The blocking minimum of the scaffold — purpose, layers, stack and application type per layer — is fixed by the platform, and the flow says which of it this flow collects.

question.description: What the engine asks directly when the stages left this gap open.

blockingDataKey.description: A datum the platform knows how to act on. Membership in the set the core knows is checked there and not here: the blocking minimum of the scaffold is fixed by the spec, but the flows of later phases bring keys of their own, and a new key must not be a breaking change to a published contract.
